provenance.status: source-only draft; no compile, GPU, default, rollback or Apex acceptance claimed; parent owns bridge, builds and all gates

device.entry: argmax_lane(x:u64, dst:u64, ncols:i64, row:i64, tid:i32, bs:i32)
device.entry_effect: per-thread lane computation plus only the listed memory/barrier effects; no return value; one block reduces exactly one row
device.call_contract: bridge launches grid=(rows,1,1), block=(bs,1,1) with bs=policy.block_size(cols) and calls the entry once per thread: x=raw byte address of contiguous F32 X element 0, dst=raw byte address of I32 output element 0, row=blockIdx.x, tid=threadIdx.x, bs=blockDim.x, ncols=ne00

imports_fx.fg169a_sloadf: sloadf(i:u64)->f32 reads shared float slot i; native shared_maxval[i], i in 0..31
imports_fx.fg169a_sstoref: sstoref(i:u64,v:f32) writes shared float slot i
imports_fx.fg169a_sloadi: sloadi(i:u64)->i32 reads shared int slot i; native shared_argmax[i], i in 0..31
imports_fx.fg169a_sstorei: sstorei(i:u64,v:i32) writes shared int slot i
imports_fx.fg169a_barrier: barrier() is __syncthreads(); entered by all threads or none since n_warps is uniform

semantics_preserved: scan over strided cols tid,tid+bs,... updates only on strict val>maxval; NaN never recorded, per-thread ties keep the earlier col

initial state maxval=-FLT_MAX (literal -340282346638528859811704183484516925440.0 = 0xFF7FFFFF) and argmax=-1; rows whose max never strictly exceeds -FLT_MAX (all -FLT_MAX or all NaN) keep the -1 sentinel
both warp reductions are shfl_xor butterflies with offsets 16,8,4,2,1 and strict >; native lane/warp reduction order kept; no fmaxf and no stable first-index rewrite

multi-warp phase: lane0 of each warp stores slot warp_id for float and int; barrier; warp0 only: lanes<n_warps reload slots, lanes>=n_warps retain their first-butterfly values exactly as native; second butterfly over all 32 lanes
store dst[row]=argmax only from warp0 lane0; shared phase skipped entirely when bs==32
device.index_policy: row, base=row*ncols and col are i64 so increments cannot wrap; argmax narrows col as! i32; policy bounds cols<=2147483647 keep it representable

host_policy.imports: none; policy is pure computation and every fg169a_ import is a device effect

entries.policy: policy(cols:i64,rows:i64)->Launch{ok:bool,bs:i32,blocks:i64,shared:i64}; single query entry, ok=false must reject before any launch effect
entries.block_size: block_size(cols:i64)->i32 is the native rule min(1024, ceil(cols/32)*32); multiple of 32, at least 32
entries.grid: grid(rows:i64)->i64 is rows, one block per row (native num_blocks=nrows)
entries.valid: valid(cols:i64,rows:i64)->bool: own bounds cols in 1..2147483647 (argmax must fit I32) and rows in 1..2147483647 (CUDA grid.x limit); then rows*cols fits i64

scope_gaps: fg169a_ bridge effects, kernel launch, stream selection and buffer span checks are parent-owned
parent must reject non-contiguous X before launch (native ggml_is_contiguous assert); the Goose policy sees only scalars
parent must provision at least 256 bytes of shared memory whenever bs>32 (32 float + 32 int slots); device never touches shared when bs==32
dst must hold at least rows I32 elements and the X span must cover rows*cols F32 elements
scalar strided scan only; no vectorization, CUB, heap, slices or sort runtime; no original numerical functions called
fn main in both files is a retained dummy; parent must not execute it
cases.json is an independent behavior contract, not an executed fixture; no test or parity claims are made here
parent_review: See review-findings.json;this contract is the original worker proposal,not the integrated ABI.
